correctness.rationale: For every a>=2, coprime 1<=d<a, and q>=1, the minimal representative in residue r modulo a is tau_r b, so membership is equivalent to j>=q tau_r+floor(d tau_r/a). An exact interval condition on j characterizes each maximal missing block. Strict monotonicity in tau proves every summand has either identically zero or exactly affine-in-q count, with nonnegative coefficients and top-run coefficient q. All edge cases are covered and an independent coin-reachability enumerator matched 3765 complete histograms; computation is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2022/2023 motivating paper treats p-Frobenius numbers for arithmetic-progression triples (primary MSC 11D07). Moree determines the total number and longest run of each two-generator semigroup and all binary polynomial coefficients; Singh–Ram determines isolated gaps. A special-family result at a=dt+1,q=1 is subsumed by the new claimed domain. Searches did not locate the complete all-length affine-in-q theorem, although the fixed-pair membership data in Moree may permit a different derivation; that possibility is explicitly recorded as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of the closest published special-family result was inaccessible; the comparison uses its detailed indexed mathematical summary.
Moree gives all binary inclusion-exclusion coefficient positions, and the affine rigidity might have appeared as an unstated or subsequently published algebraic consequence.
A specialized literature result or table using the synonymous term deserts may not have been indexed by the performed searches.

value.rationale: Maximal missing intervals (deserts) are a natural named numerical-semigroup invariant. The theorem gives the full exact length-resolved histogram for all two-generator semigroups, showing unexpected linearity and support stability across any fixed residue class b mod a, including the exact multiplicity of the longest run. Earlier literature focuses on total counts, maximal length and isolated gaps, leaving the joint full parameter-dependent structure mathematically motivated.
